content: Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when spending time outdoors to minimize sun exposure. This medication is chemically similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under the age of 18 should not take aspirin or aspirin-related medications (such as salicylates) if they have chickenpox, the flu, any undiagnosed illness, or if they have recently received a vaccine, as this may increase the risk of serious complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary and prescribed by a healthcare provider. It is known to pass into breast milk and may cause undesirable effects in a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before use if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Mesalamine is closely related to other medications such as balsalazide, olsalazine, and sulfasalazine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially leading to false test results. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel if you are taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests, may be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during treatment to monitor your health. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If the medication bottle contains a desiccant, keep the desiccant in the bottle to maintain product stability. Always tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, or joint and muscle pain. Occasionally, you may notice whole or partial tablets or capsules in your stool. If this occurs frequently, inform your doctor. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, mesalamine may worsen ulcerative colitis. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately.
